"""Layer-0 MLP down_proj, component 4736: a "-er fragment" detector.

What it does: this component reads the current token and writes a small signed
value into the residual stream. It is negative on short word-piece fragments that
end in "er" (fer, ser, ker, ber, ver, mer, ter, her, zer, ger, cher, ...) and on a
few related pieces (ke, ze, pet, ven, bed, hel), in names and technical words that
are split across tokens; it is positive on a few frequent tokens and pieces such as
"</tool_response>", "ogen" and "施". Everything else is 0. Each value is the mean
activation of that token class over training text, so the prediction is the
per-class average.

Why this shape: the activation depends mostly on the token itself; no simple
context rule was found (checked: word position, capitalisation, script).
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Word-piece fragments ending in "er" (with an optional leading space and one letter).
ER_FRAGMENT = re.compile(r" ?[A-Za-z]?(s|k|b|v|f|m|t|h|z|g|ch)er|ke|ze|pet| ?ven|bed|hel", re.I)
ER_VALUE = -0.073

# The most influential single tokens outside that class (mean activation).
TOKEN_VALUE = {
    "er": -0.08, "SED": -0.18, "</tool_response>": 0.11, " pet": -0.22, "ERV": -0.13,
    "<|im_end|>": -0.04, " вер": -0.29, " against": -0.08, " than": 0.05, " ket": -0.53,
    " really": -0.09, "www": -0.11, " real": 0.07, " still": 0.07, "ogen": 0.18,
    " complex": 0.09, " between": 0.04, "вер": -0.20, " respectively": 0.11,
    " Hel": -0.28, " Pet": -0.16, " area": 0.06, " food": -0.08, "://": -0.05,
    " why": -0.08, "施": 0.20,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if ER_FRAGMENT.fullmatch(token):
        return carry, ER_VALUE
    return carry, TOKEN_VALUE.get(token, 0.0)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4737: predicts (essentially) nothing.

This component reads the layer-0 MLP hidden state along one direction and writes a
fixed vector into the residual stream. Its activation is sign-mixed and small (RMS 0.035),
and it is nearly silent in the model: switching it off changes the next-token distribution
by about 5e-6 nats per position. Its value is set by the identity of the current token
(a token table explains about 20-28% of its variance on held-out text), but no
word-level concept I tried does: token classes such as CJK, Cyrillic, punctuation,
leading-space words, or camelCase/dotted code identifiers all have means near zero with
wide spread in both signs. So this program predicts the component's typical value, 0,
which is the same as switching it off.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Code-expression endings, and the whitespace between source statements.

The main positive cases are closing parentheses or square brackets at a line
end, especially in Python-like, unpunctuated source. Calls, assignments, empty
argument/list syntax and a closing delimiter on its own line strengthen this
signal. Plain line breaks and following indentation get smaller predictions.
Recent semicolon/braced source weakens it; quoted/interpolated closers have
separate gains. Ordinary word tokens are zero. This is a surface-syntax
approximation, not a parser: it misses lexical and longer-context variation.
"""
import re

READS = ()
ASSIGN = re.compile(r'(?<![<>=!:])=(?!=)|:=')
CALL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.\w+)*\(')
STATEMENT = re.compile(r'^(return|break|continue|raise|yield|import|from|assert|del)\b')
PYTHON = re.compile(
    r'^(def |class |from \w+ import |import |if .*:|elif .*:|else:|'
    r'for .*:|while .*:|try:|except|with .*:)|\bself\.')
PLAIN_CODE = re.compile(
    r'^(?:[ \t]*#+)?[ \t]*(?:[A-Za-z_]\w*\s*=(?!=)|'
    r'\w+\.\w+\(|print\(|return\b)')
PYTHON_BLOCK = re.compile(
    r'^(def \w+\(|class \w+.*:|from \w+ import |if .*:|for .*:|while .*:)')


def source_features(line):
    # Ignore the line-number/tab prefix of printed source listings.
    text = re.sub(r'^\s*\d+\t', '', line).strip()
    style = (bool(PYTHON.search(text)) and not text.endswith(';')) or (
        bool(PLAIN_CODE.match(text)) and not text.endswith((';', '{', '}')))
    return (style, bool(ASSIGN.search(text)), bool(CALL.search(text)),
            bool(STATEMENT.match(text)))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, token = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if start:
        carry = (doc, '', 0.0, 0.0, False, False)
    _, line, style_memory, semicolons, previous_open, previous_break = carry
    # Escaped newlines in quoted code update context, but aren't real line breaks.
    parts = (line + token.replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\r', '')).split('\n')
    if len(parts) == 1 and any(c.isalnum() for c in token):
        return (doc, parts[0][-300:], style_memory, semicolons,
                previous_open, False), 0.0
    style, assignment, call, statement = source_features(parts[0])
    style = float(style or style_memory > .4)
    alone = not line.strip()
    core = token.replace('\r', '').rstrip('\n')
    ending = core.strip()
    quote = '"' in ending or "'" in ending
    leading = core.startswith(' ')
    value = 0.0
    if '\n' in token or token == '\r':
        if not ending:
            if ' ' in core or '\t' in core:
                value = .40 + .64*style - .36*leading - .23*semicolons
            else:
                value = (.04 + 1.26*statement + .40*style + .40*assignment
                         + .70*start - .13*semicolons)
        elif (not ending.endswith((';', ':', ','))
              and not any(c.isalnum() for c in ending)):
            if ending.endswith(')'):
                value = (.29 + .86*style + .69*call + .55*('()' in ending)
                         - .54*semicolons + .99*alone + .26*assignment)
            elif ending.endswith(']'):
                value = (.64 + 1.06*style + 1.21*('[]' in ending)
                         + .61*alone - .27*semicolons)
            elif ending.endswith('}'):
                value = .33 + .40*style - .32*semicolons - .08*leading
            elif ending in ('"', "'", '""', "''"):
                value = .58 + .40*style + .27*assignment - .29*semicolons
    elif token and all(c in ' \t' for c in token) and len(token) > 1:
        if alone:
            value = (-.04 + .43*style - .21*previous_open - .20*semicolons
                     - .15*(len(token) <= 2) + .26*previous_break)
    elif ending and not any(c.isalnum() for c in ending):
        if ending.rstrip('\\').endswith(')'):
            interpolation = bool(re.search(r'''}["']''', ending))
            value = (-.09 + .32*quote + .27*style + 1.26*interpolation
                     + .15*call + .063*min(len(token), 16))
        elif ending.endswith(']'):
            value = (.26 + .46*quote + .42*style
                     - .24*(ending == ']') - .44*('\\' in token))
    # Remember bounded line text, unfinished delimiters, and recent source style.
    for ended in parts[:-1]:
        bare = re.sub(r'^\s*\d+\t', '', ended).strip()
        if bare.endswith(';'):
            semicolons = 1.0
        elif bare.endswith('{'):
            semicolons = max(.7, semicolons)
        else:
            semicolons *= .96
        if PYTHON_BLOCK.match(bare):
            semicolons = 0.0
        style_memory = max(.85*style_memory, float(source_features(ended)[0]))
        if bare:
            previous_open = ended.rstrip().endswith(('(', '[', '{', ','))
    carry = (doc, parts[-1][-300:], style_memory, semicolons,
             previous_open, '\n' in token)
    return carry, float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Layer-0 MLP feature (down_proj unit 4738): the newline that ends an indented line of code.

It fires on a newline token whose line ends in a closing bracket or quote, such as ')\\n',
']\\n', '"\\n', "'\\n", '()\\n' or '")\\n', and on whitespace-only lines ('    \\n'). It is weak
at the top level of a file and strong inside a block: the deeper the indentation of the
line that the newline ends, the larger the activation. Other tokens predict 0.

Values are the typical activations, scaled by 0.8 (the best fit to the measured activation).
"""

READS = ()

CLOSERS = set(')]"\'')


def _indent(line):
    # Leading whitespace width of a line, a tab counting as four spaces.
    width = 0
    for ch in line:
        if ch == " ":
            width += 1
        elif ch == "\t":
            width += 4
        else:
            break
    return width


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if "\n" not in tok:
        return carry, 0.0
    body = tok.rstrip(" \t\r\n")
    # The line this newline ends: the text since the previous newline, through this token.
    before = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-40:-1]).rsplit("\n", 1)[-1]
    depth = _indent(before + body)
    if body == "":
        value = 0.08 if depth < 4 else 0.32
    elif body[-1] in CLOSERS:
        value = 0.32 if depth < 4 else (1.04 if depth < 8 else 1.28)
    else:
        value = 0.04 if depth < 4 else 0.24
    return carry, value

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a lowercase-word restart signal.

The first lowercase token after a period, colon, dash, or line break gets a
positive pulse; ordinary word continuations and commas get almost none.
Grammatical word classes scale the pulse. Single letters, code words, and
mixed-case identifiers are weaker. Uppercase starts are left near zero.
Conversation delimiters have separate signed responses. Only the previous
token is retained, and it is forgotten at document changes.
"""
import unicodedata

READS = ()

# Each familiar word class supplies (pulse multiplier, small baseline).
WORD_CLASSES = (
    ('the', 1.672, 0.009),                         # definite article
    ('a an', 1.073, -0.001),                      # indefinite articles
    ('this that these those', 1.535, 0.005),       # demonstratives
    ('you he she it we they me him her us them', 1.670, 0.023),
    ('and or nor', 1.425, -0.004),                 # coordinators
    ('but so if because although though however therefore then thus '
     'yet nevertheless unless since while when whenever until once',
     1.595, -0.004),                              # clause connectives
    ('no not never neither', 1.487, 0.010),        # negation
    ('of in on at to for from with by as into over under through',
     1.218, 0.001),                               # prepositions
    ('return def class import const var function true false null none '
     'int str bool string float void public private protected static '
     'console print println logger else break continue undefined boolean '
     'http https sqrt', 0.353, -0.051),            # code and type words
)
WORD_CLASSES = tuple((frozenset(w.split()), f, b) for w, f, b in WORD_CLASSES)

# Boundary characters grouped by their ordinary textual role.
PULSES = (
    ('.', 1.279), (':', 0.757), (';', 0.470),
    ('—–-', 0.829), ('?', 0.987), ('!', 0.767),
    ('|', 0.522), ('#', 0.838), ('•·', 0.793),
    ('→', 0.643), ('/\\', 0.742), ('%', 0.195),
    (')]}', 0.128), ('([{', 0.008), ('"\'“”‘’', 0.054),
    ('=+*<>~≈', 0.163), (',', 0.012),
)
LINE_END_PULSES = {'.': 0.817, ':': 0.529, '?': 0.782, '!': 0.740}


def word_scale(word):
    for words, factor, baseline in WORD_CLASSES:
        if word in words:
            return factor, baseline
    if not word.isalpha() or not word.islower(): return 0.368, -0.028
    if 'LATIN' not in unicodedata.name(word[0], ''): return 0.856, 0.001
    if len(word) == 1: return 0.586, -0.005
    if len(word) <= 3: return 0.925, -0.004
    return 1.0, -0.001


def restart_pulse(previous, current):
    tail = previous.rstrip()
    if not tail:
        if '\n' in previous: return 0.305
        return 0.075 if len(previous) > 1 else 0.208
    separated = current[:1].isspace() or tail != previous
    if not separated and not tail.endswith(('—', '–', '(', '[', '"', '“')):
        return -0.007
    last = tail[-1]
    if '\n' in previous:
        if last in LINE_END_PULSES: return LINE_END_PULSES[last]
        if '\n' in previous[len(tail):]: return 0.305
    if tail.endswith('->'): return 0.643
    for characters, pulse in PULSES:
        if last in characters: return pulse
    return -0.007 if last.isalnum() else 0.080


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, token = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else None
    word = token.strip()
    value = -0.003
    period_before = previous is not None and previous.rstrip().endswith('.')
    if token == '</think>': value = -0.63
    elif token == '<|im_end|>': value = 0.34 if period_before else -0.31
    elif token == '<|im_start|>':
        value = -0.04 if previous and '\n' in previous else -0.40
    elif token == '</tool_response>': value = 0.79 if period_before else 0.19
    elif token in ('<tool_response>', '</tool_call>'): value = -0.15
    elif token == '<tool_call>': value = 0.10
    elif previous is not None and word and word[0].islower():
        factor, baseline = word_scale(word)
        value = baseline + restart_pulse(previous, token) * factor
        if token.startswith('\t'): value = -0.12
    return (doc, token), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 4739: a "new phrase after punctuation" detector.

What it does, in plain terms: the component is quiet on almost every token. It switches on
for a plain word that comes right after punctuation (a period, colon, dash, arrow, pipe,
bracket, semicolon...), i.e. the first word of a new clause or list item. It switches on
harder when that word is a function word (the, a, and, in, but, this, to, we, it...) and
hardest when the punctuation is sentence-final (. ! ?): "... downtown. [so] ...".
Inside a run of ordinary words, and at the start of a document, it predicts 0.

The numbers are small weights (fitted on 2048 training rows, shrunk by 0.2 because the
full fit overshoots on held-out rows); the rule is a
concept, not a lookup of token ids, so the table of function words is the only list.
"""

READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = set(
    "the a an this these that those every each some no "
    "and but so then although if as because while when or "
    "in to of at on for with from by "
    "we i it he she they you there is was are were be been".split()
)
SENTENCE_END = set(".!?")
# Least-squares fit (x0.2 shrink, since full-size predictions overshoot: VE<0).
WORD_AFTER_PUNCT = 0.011
FUNCTION_BONUS = 0.010
SENTENCE_BONUS = 0.087


def _is_punct(s):
    """True if the token ends in punctuation (not a letter, digit or space)."""
    end = s.rstrip()[-1:]
    return end != "" and not end.isalnum()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = cur.strip()
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if not (_is_punct(prev) and word.isalpha()):
        return None, 0.0
    value = WORD_AFTER_PUNCT
    if word.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value += FUNCTION_BONUS
        if prev.rstrip()[-1:] in SENTENCE_END:
            value += SENTENCE_BONUS
    return None, value

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4741 — a few readable situations, in plain terms.

This component is mostly quiet (near 0) and speaks up in three situations:

1. Opening a JSON tool call. The token `{"` (and the markup around tool calls,
   `<tool_call>`, `<think>`, `<tool_response>`) pushes it negative, about -0.3.
   This is the most reliable, high-importance behaviour in the component.
2. Text that has been garbled into byte-level noise. When the last few tokens
   contain NUL bytes (UTF-16-style text written with a NUL between every letter),
   the next letter is strongly positive (about +1.2).
3. Backslash-escaped UTF-8 (for example a curly apostrophe written as literal
   `\\xe2\\x80\\x99`), the letter that follows is positive (about +1.0).

Everywhere else it predicts 0. The rest of its variance is small, diffuse,
token-level noise that a short rule cannot capture.
"""

READS = ()

# Markup tokens that push the component negative.
MARKUP = {
    '{"': -0.32,
    '<think>': -0.26,
    '<tool_response>': -0.19,
    '</tool_response>': -0.19,
    '<tool_call>': -0.08,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    cur = toks[-1]
    # The up to 8 tokens before this one, stopping at a document boundary.
    recent = []
    for i in range(len(toks) - 2, max(-1, len(toks) - 9), -1):
        if docs[i] != docs[-1]:
            break
        recent.append(toks[i])
    nul_count = sum(1 for s in recent if s == "\x00")
    escape_count = sum(1 for s in recent if "\\x" in s)
    is_letter = len(cur) == 1 and cur.isascii() and cur.isalpha()

    if cur in MARKUP:
        return carry, MARKUP[cur]
    if nul_count >= 3 and cur != "\x00":
        # Letters inside NUL-interleaved (UTF-16-like) text.
        return carry, 1.2 if is_letter else 0.1
    if escape_count >= 3 and is_letter and cur.islower():
        # Letter right after backslash-hex escaped UTF-8.
        return carry, 1.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Estimate the component on recurring chat and JSON boundary tokens.

The largest repeated negative responses are to the JSON opener, reasoning markers,
and tool-call/response markers. A fresh document that starts with the chat
message-start token has its own small negative response. Other positions get zero;
this misses scattered word-specific responses.
"""

READS = ()

CHAT_MARKERS = {
    '{"': -0.323,
    "{\n": -0.055,
    "<tool_call>": -0.085,
    "</think>": -0.089,
    "<think>": -0.261,
    "<tool_response>": -0.193,
    "</tool_response>": -0.195,
    "<|im_end|>": -0.036,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    del carry, upstream
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    at_new_document = (
        len(prefix.token_ids) > 1
        and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if token == "<|im_start|>" and at_new_document:
        return None, -0.073

"""Cleaning-word detector for MLP neuron-direction layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4742.

This component fires on words about cleaning and hygiene. Its strongest response is to
the word "clean" itself (" clean", " cleaned", " cleaning", " cleaner"), which pushes
the activation to about 5-7. Weaker responses come from related words that also mean
wiping, washing, purifying or removing dirt (wash, sanitize, dirty, purify, flush, wet,
dry, filter, 洗澡, 清理). Words about checking or validating code and data (check,
validation, lint, eslint) give a small response of about 0.6. Everything else is about 0.

The program looks only at the current token, so it has no carry.
"""

CLEAN_CORE = {"clean", "cleaned", "cleaning", "cleaner", "cleanse", "cleans", "cleanup",
              "cleanly", "cleanliness"}
CLEAN_RELATED = {"wash", "washed", "washing", "sanitize", "sanitized", "sanitizing",
                 "sanitary", "dirty", "purification", "purified", "purify", "purifier",
                 "flush", "wet", "dry", "filter", "filtered", "filtering", "fresh", "wipe",
                 "scrub", "disinfect", "contaminant", "contaminants",
                 "洗澡", "清理", "清洁", "清洗", "净化", "干净", "纯", "洗", "干", "清"}
CHECKING = {"check", "checks", "checked", "checking", "validation", "validate",
            "validated", "validator", "lint", "eslint"}

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in CLEAN_CORE:
        value = 6.0
    elif word in CLEAN_RELATED:
        value = 1.4
    elif word in CHECKING:
        value = 0.6
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""A local phonetic-transition approximation.

The largest responses often bridge an i-like or palatal syllable and a new vowel,
across several writing systems.  This program classifies those endings
and vowel onsets, with small corrections for first-person constructions.
It deliberately ignores most weak, token-specific background responses.
"""
READS = ()

# Kana encode their vowel in their conventional syllabic spelling.
FRONT_KANA = set('いぃきぎしじちぢにひびぴみりイィキギシジチヂニヒビピミリ')
E_KANA = set('えぇけげせぜてでねへべぺめれエェケゲセゼテデネヘベペメレ')
# Common Chinese characters read with an i-like final, including names.
FRONT_HAN = set(
    '里理李莉丽麗利力历歷礼禮黎璃离離梨立粒厘'
    '西希席习習锡錫喜细細系息熙惜'
    '迪地弟第低底帝蒂敌敵笛递遞'
    '尼泥妮倪你米密秘弥彌迷咪'
    '伊依衣医醫一亿億意易义義艺藝宜仪儀移亦益忆憶'
    '基机機几幾及即级級集极極吉济濟纪紀记記计計鸡雞技季姬'
    '皮疲匹批披僻庇币幣碧比毕畢'
    '维維韦韋伟偉卫衛薇菲飞飛非斐'
)


def front_ending(s):
    """A spelling-based approximation to i-like or palatal syllables."""
    if not s:
        return False
    c = s[-1]
    if c in FRONT_KANA or c in FRONT_HAN or c in 'iIíìîïİıиИіІїЇйЙιίيیىิีिी':
        return True
    if '\uac00' <= c <= '\ud7a3':
        # Open Hangul syllables with i, wi, ui, or a y-glide vowel.
        return (ord(c) - 0xac00) % 28 == 0 and (
            ((ord(c) - 0xac00) // 28) % 21 in (2, 3, 6, 7, 16, 17, 19, 20)
        )
    return False


# Each vowel fragment has a base response, an i-ending bonus, and a ri bonus.
# Small kana attach to a consonant and need not behave like full-sized vowels.
KATA_VOWELS = {
    'ア': (0.314, 0.606, 0.164),
    'ァ': (0.314, 0.186, 0.256),
    'エ': (0.098, 0.218, 0.403),
    'ェ': (-0.045, 0.186, 0.256),
    'オ': (0.155, 0.462, 0.433),
    'ォ': (0.056, 0.186, 0.256),
    'ウ': (0.141, 0.355, 0.310),
    'ゥ': (-0.028, 0.186, 0.256),
    'ヤ': (0.068, 0.473, 0.416),
    'ャ': (0.033, 0.190, 0.153),
    'ユ': (-0.029, 0.186, 0.256),
    'ュ': (-0.142, 0.186, 0.256),
    'ヨ': (0.138, 0.186, 0.256),
    'ョ': (-0.067, 0.186, 0.256),
}


def local_response(previous, token):
    p = previous[-1:] if previous else ''
    s = token.strip()
    front = front_ending(previous)
    e_kana = bool(p and p in E_KANA)
    ri = bool(p and p in 'リり')
    multi_letter = (front and len(previous.strip()) > 1
                    and previous[-2].isalpha())
    korean_i = (bool(p) and '\uac00' <= p <= '\ud7a3'
                and (ord(p) - 0xac00) % 588 == 20 * 28)
    joined = bool(token and not token[0].isspace())
    value = 0.0011
    if joined and 0 < len(token) <= 2:
        onset = token[0]
        if onset in KATA_VOWELS and (len(token) == 1 or token[-1] in 'ンー'):

"""Score the beginning of direct speech, especially dialogue in a narrative.

Opening quotes get larger values after sentence boundaries or speech tags.
The last 64 tokens supply simple dialogue cues: personal pronouns, speech verbs,
and faces/gestures. Certain quote-ending punctuation gets a smaller response.
Code-like punctuation downweights the background dialogue score. This does
not try to reproduce the small, idiosyncratic activations on ordinary words.
"""
from collections import deque
from functools import lru_cache

FIRST_SECOND = set('''

mình ngươi ta tôi chúng je tu nous vous ich du wir ihr yo tú nosotros
я ты мы вы
'''.split())
THIRD_PERSON = set('''

il elle ils elles er sie ihn ihm lui él ella ellos ellas
он она они его её их
'''.split())
SPEECH = set('''

reply replies replied answer answers answered whisper whispers whispered
shout shouts shouted cry cries cried crying exclaim exclaims exclaimed
remark remarked respond responded called muttered murmured explained
continued declared consoled chuckled nói hỏi đáp dit dit-il demanda répondit
sagte fragte antwortete
'''.split())
GESTURES = set('''
look looked looking smile smiled smiling nod nodded nodding
shake shook shaking laugh laughed laughing sigh sighed sighing
stare stared staring turn turned turning eyes face lips voice hand hands
head mouth smirk smirked shoulders shoulder glanced gaze gazed frowned
blinked shrugged
'''.split())
CODE = set('{}[]();=\\`<>')


@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def cues(s):
    word = s.strip().lower().strip('.,!?;:"\'“”‘’«»()[]')
    return (
        word in FIRST_SECOND or any(c in s for c in '我你您咱俺吾'),
        word in THIRD_PERSON or any(c in s for c in '他她它'),
        word in SPEECH or any(c in s for c in '说說问問答喊叫曰道'),
        word in GESTURES or any(c in s for c in '笑叹嘆眼脸臉瞧望眉摇搖头頭声聲'),
        min(sum(c in CODE for c in s), 3),
        sum(c in '"“”«»' for c in s),
    )


def opening_quote(s):
    w = s.strip()
    if w in ("'", "''"):
        return "'", '', '', False
    for i, mark in enumerate(w):
        if mark not in '"“„«‘':
            continue
        before, after = w[:i], w[i+1:]
        if before not in ('', ',', '，', '.', '。', ':', '：', '、'):
            return None
        if mark == '"' and before:
            return None  # punctuation followed by an ASCII closing quote
        if after and not after[0].isalpha() and after[0] not in '…—-':
            return None
        return mark, before, after, s[:1].isspace()
    return None

    doc, s = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]

    else:
        _, history, previous = carry

    w = s.strip()

    if len(w) >= 2 and w[1] in '"”':
        if w[0] in '。！？':
            value = .31
        elif w[0] in '?!':
            value = .10 if '\n' in s else .18
        elif w[0] in ',，':
            value = .14
    elif w in ('”', '»'):

    if quote is not None:
        mark, before, after, space = quote
        n = max(len(history), 16)
        first, third, speech, body, code, quotes = (
            sum(row[j] for row in history)/n for j in range(6)
        )
        people = min(first + 1.5*third, .30)
        speech, body, quotes = min(speech, .08), min(body, .08), min(quotes, .15)
        prose = max(0., 1.-5.*code)
        tail = previous.rstrip()
        end = ('\n' in previous or tail.endswith(('.', '。', '?', '？', '!', '！'))
               or before in ('.', '。'))
        comma = tail.endswith((',', '，')) or before in (',', '，')
        colon = tail.endswith((':', '：')) or before in (':', '：')
        closed = tail.endswith(('”', '»', '"', "''"))

        value = -.10 + .18*fused + .57*(before == '：') + .14*(mark == '„')
        value += end*(-.01 + 2.1*people + 6.4*speech + 9.9*body + .36*prose)
        value += comma*(.07 + 1.7*people + 8.2*speech)
        value += colon*(2.*people + 3.4*speech)
        value += closed*(.23 + 3.4*people)
        value += 3.*quotes*(mark == '“')

"""Sentence-end detector for layers.0.mlp.down_proj, component 4756.

What it does: the component fires on tokens that end a sentence or a document,
mostly in Chinese and Japanese text, and is near zero everywhere else.

- The CJK full stop 。 is the strongest trigger, and so is <|endoftext|>, the
  token that separates packed documents.
- 。 fused with a line break (one token, e.g. "。\\n") fires less.
- The other CJK sentence-final marks ！ ？ ； fire moderately.
- Ordinary ASCII punctuation (. ! ?), commas and ordinary words do not fire.
- Just after a document starts the response is stronger: about 2x at its first
  token, about 1.5x at 20 tokens, about 1.2x at 100 tokens.

The values are predicted activations in the component's own units.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

FULL_STOP = 1.3          # 。 alone or fused with other non-newline characters (e.g. 。（)
FULL_STOP_NEWLINE = 0.6  # 。 fused with a line break (e.g. 。\n)
OTHER_CJK_STOPS = 0.5    # ！ ？ ； (and tokens containing them, e.g. ！”)
END_OF_TEXT = 1.2        # <|endoftext|>

BOOST_SCALE = 20.0       # start-of-document boost: 1 + BOOST_SCALE / (BOOST_SCALE + distance)


def base_value(token: str) -> float:
    if token == "<|endoftext|>":
        return END_OF_TEXT
    if "。" in token:
        return FULL_STOP_NEWLINE if "\n" in token else FULL_STOP
    if any(mark in token for mark in "！？；"):
        return OTHER_CJK_STOPS
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: index of the first token of the current document (None at a row's first token).
    start = 0 if carry is None else carry
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        start = prefix.position  # a new document starts at this token
    distance = prefix.position - start  # tokens since the document started
    boost = 1.0 + BOOST_SCALE / (BOOST_SCALE + distance)
    return start, float(base_value(prefix.token_strings[-1]) * boost)

word beginnings, especially capitalized beginnings and vowel junctions.

prefixes give a weak negative response. Indented blank lines are negative,
with a softer response at four-column indentation widths.

frequent misspelling "Huamn". Other token-specific variation is not modeled.

    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

        _, previous, began_word = carry

        spaces = len(s) - len(s.lstrip(' '))
        width = spaces + 4 * s.count('\t')
        value = -0.54 * min(max(width - 1, 0) / 12, 1)
        if width % 4 == 0:
            value *= 0.75

        value = -0.01 if len(s) >= 2 else 0.0
        match = re.search(r'([^\W\d_]+)$', previous)
        p = match.group() if match else ''
        word_start = began_word or len(p) < len(previous)
        if p.isupper() and len(p) == 1:
            value = -0.05

                if p[0].lower() in VOWELS and n > 1:

            elif p.islower():
                value = (0.13, 0.03, 0.0)[n - 1]
            elif p.isupper():
                value = (0.17, 0.015, -0.04)[n - 1]
        # A capital in mid-word usually starts a new CamelCase word.

            value = -0.01

attached to a word. Qwen-style tokenizers split numbers into single digits and leave the
space in front of them as a separate token, so "in 1906" is "in", " ", "1", "9", "0", "6".

a digit-like continuation) comes next. Its strength depends on the token before the space:
after a word ("in", "of", "the", "from", "about", ...) it is strong, after "=" or another
operator it is medium, after a digit, comma or colon it is weaker, after an indentation
it is weak, and after a newline or a period it is off. A space glued to the start of a
non-Latin character (" " + a partial UTF-8 byte) also fires, moderately. Every other token
is about 0.

component's mean activation for each class on the training rows.

AFTER_OPERATOR = 1.2  # "x = 2", "a + 3", "- 4"
AFTER_DIGIT_OR_PUNCT = 1.0  # "0 5", "1, 2", "10: 3"
AFTER_INDENT = 0.5  # a space after an indentation token
AFTER_PERIOD = 0.15  # sentence start: near off
AFTER_NEWLINE = 0.0  # line start: off

    """The token before the newest one, or None at the start of a document."""
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None

    if prev is None:
        return AFTER_PERIOD
    if "\n" in prev:
        return AFTER_NEWLINE
    if prev == ".":

    if prev.strip() == "":

        return "letter"

            word = (word + piece.lower())[-64:]
        elif word:
            non_ascii = any(ord(char) > 127 for char in word)

            english = 0.85 * english + float(word in ENGLISH_CUES)
            word = ""
    evidence = foreign / (foreign + english + 0.15)
    confidence = min(1.0, max(0.0, (evidence - 0.4) / 0.4))

    value = PARTICLES.get(token, 0.0)
    if token.startswith(" "):
        link = token[1:]
        if link in SHARED:
            ordinary, multilingual = SHARED[link]
            value = ordinary + confidence * (multilingual - ordinary)
        elif link in LINKS:
            value = LINKS[link]
        elif link.isalpha() and len(link) <= 2:
            names = [unicodedata.name(char, "") for char in link]
            if any("CYRILLIC" in name for name in names):
                value = -0.18 if link.islower() else -0.07
            elif any("ARABIC" in name for name in names):
                value = -0.17
            elif any("GREEK" in name for name in names):
                value = -0.32
        if value < -0.15 and (link not in ENGLISH_CUES or link in SHARED):
            value *= PAUSE_SCALE[previous]

    carry = (doc, word, foreign, english, ending_kind(token, previous))
    return carry, float(value)

"""Negative activation on prepositions and function words of non-English languages.

The component writes a strongly negative value at a word that opens a non-English phrase,
so that the word's neighbours are read as "in a foreign phrase". Its size depends on the word:

- Russian and Arabic-script prepositions (на, по, для, к, с, в; على, في, من, ل, ب): about -2.2.
- Prepositions of Romance, German, Dutch, Scandinavian and other languages (de, en, con,
  di, à, pour, auf, zu, med, för, na, på): about -1.2.
- 'and' in other languages (и, und, ve, och, و): about -1.0.
- Articles (la, les, el, des, der, die, un, eine, ال): about -0.7.
- Some English prepositions (under, among, across, against, via, per): about -0.6.
- English-looking 'a', 'an', 'in' (Spanish a, Italian in, German in): about -0.5, but only
  when the nearby words are not English.

A word right after punctuation (a clause start) is weakened to about a third. English
'to, of, for, with, on, at, from, by' stay at zero.
Only word-initial tokens (with a leading space) count, plus the Japanese particles の and で,
which have no leading space and get -0.8.
"""

READS = ()

PUNCTUATION = set(',.;:!?()[]{}"\'«»“”‘’-–—/')

SLAVIC_ARABIC = set(
    """в во на с со к по из от за при для о у до под над про между без ко через
    على إلى من في عن مع ل ب""".split()
)
PREPOSITIONS = set(
    """der des de en con di del della nel nella nei dell aux au à sur pour dans par para
    por zur zum zu auf für mit bei aus von über unter nach als durch em com entre van voor
    naar aan med från till för av om sobre contre sans avec vers chez ao trong với về cho
    untuk dengan pada ke ve na з på da př об""".split()
)
ARTICLES = set(
    """la les el los las il le die das den dem eine einer einen eines ein
    un une uno um uma delle dei dell ال لل بال al du im az τ""".split()
)
CONJUNCTIONS = set("и und ve och و".split())
ENGLISH_RARE = set(
    "under among amongst across against via within towards regarding per between over".split()
)
ENGLISH_WORDS = set(
    """the of and to is in a that it for with was on as be by this are at
    from or not you an have which they were he she his her""".split()
)
JAPANESE = set("の で".split())
AMBIGUOUS = set("a an in".split())


def english_share(prefix):
    """Share of English function words among the last 24 words of this document."""
    n = english = 0
    i = len(prefix.token_ids) - 2
    while i >= 0 and i >= len(prefix.token_ids) - 25:
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
            break
        word = prefix.token_strings[i].strip().lower()
        if word:
            n += 1
            english += word in ENGLISH_WORDS
        i -= 1
    return english / n if n else 1.0


def after_punctuation(prefix):
    """True when the word before the current token is punctuation (a clause boundary)."""
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return False
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    return before != "" and all(ch in PUNCTUATION for ch in before)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    if not token.startswith(" "):
        return carry, (-0.8 if token in JAPANESE else 0.0)
    if word != word.lower():
        return carry, 0.0
    if word in SLAVIC_ARABIC:
        value = -2.2
    elif word in PREPOSITIONS:
        value = -1.2
    elif word in CONJUNCTIONS:
        value = -1.0
    elif word in ARTICLES:
        value = -0.7
    elif word in ENGLISH_RARE:
        value = -0.6
    elif word in AMBIGUOUS and english_share(prefix) < 0.05:
        value = -0.5
    else:
        return carry, 0.0
    if after_punctuation(prefix):
        value *= 0.35
    return carry, value

The examples point to prepositions and case/linking particles: they are named
by their spelling rather than by token number. Unlisted tokens contribute zero.

"""Layer-0 MLP down_proj component 4790 (v3).

Negative on tokens that are pieces of a *written-out* byte or character code, and on a few
chat-structure tokens. Mostly zero everywhere else.

- A literal escape "\\xe2\\x80\\x99" is split into tokens; the piece that opens an escape
  for a non-ASCII byte is strongly negative: "\\xe" (3-byte lead) most, then "\\xc" (2-byte
  lead), a bare "\\x", and "\\xa"/"\\xb" (continuation bytes) less.
- The chat/tool markers "<tool_call>" and "<|im_end|>" are negative; the end of a turn is
  most negative after prose and near zero after a tool call.
- NUL characters that follow a letter (UTF-16-style text such as "h\\x00a\\x00t") are negative.
- An escaped quote that opens an f-string inside code, "(f\\"", is negative.
- "</tool_response>" is mildly positive.
"""
READS = ()

HEX_ESCAPE = {"\\xe": -2.1, "\\xc": -1.6, "\\xb": -0.8, "\\xa": -0.6, "\\x": -0.9}
OTHER = {
    "<tool_call>": -1.3,
    "\\'": -0.9,
    "&#": -0.6,
    " &#": -0.4,
    "xe": -0.4,
    "</tool_response>": 0.35,
    "</tool_call>": -0.15,
    "</think>": -0.12,
    "\\t": -0.09,
}
# Turn-end token after: a tool-call close, a tool-response close, or prose (default).
IM_END_AFTER = {"</tool_call>": -0.3, "</tool_response>": -0.5}
SENTENCE_END = {".", "?", "!", "。", ")", "]", '"'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if tok in HEX_ESCAPE:
        return carry, HEX_ESCAPE[tok]
    if tok == "<|im_end|>":
        if prev in IM_END_AFTER:
            return carry, IM_END_AFTER[prev]
        return carry, -1.1 if prev[-1:] in SENTENCE_END else -0.8
    if tok == "\x00":
        return carry, 0.0 if prev in ("", " ") else -0.6
    if tok == '\\"':
        return carry, -0.9 if prev == "(f" else -0.2
    return carry, OTHER.get(tok, 0.0)

The large response belongs to the token's literal (), not to a parsed call.
Attached line endings and closing delimiters reduce it; member access, indexing
and escape/backtick continuations increase it. Empty braces, empty square
brackets, and period-comma tokens receive smaller fixed responses. Other
tokens outside these delimiter patterns receive zero.

        value -= 0.8 * len(before.strip()) + 2.5 * ('(' in before)
        value -= 0.9 * ('\n' in s) + 0.5 * max(s.count('\n') - 1, 0)
        value -= 0.8 * after.count(')')
        value -= (0.3 if '\n' in s else 0.6) * (';' in after)
        value -= 0.25 * (',' in after)
        value += (0.05 if '\n' in s else -0.25) * (':' in after)
        value -= 1.2 * ('{' in after) + 0.8 * ('}' in after)
        value += (0.25 if ')' not in after else -0.65) * ('.' in after)
        value += 1.0 * ('\\' in after or '`' in after)
        value += 0.85 * ('->' in after) + 0.8 * ('[' in after)
        value = max(0.0, value)
    elif '{}' in s:
        value = 1.0
    elif '[]' in s:
        value = 0.35
    elif ')' in s or '）' in s:
        value = 0.4 if not any(c.isalnum() for c in s) else 0.0

"""Layer-0 MLP component 4796 (down_proj): an "Arabic word starts here" detector.

In plain terms, it fires:
- Strongly on the first token of an Arabic-script word: a token such as " ت" or " من"
  (a space followed by an Arabic letter), when the text around it is Arabic. Its size
  depends on the word's first letter. Words opening with alif (including the article
  "ال") are weak, words opening with a letter that does not join to the next one
  (د ذ ر ز و) are medium, and other letters are strong.
- Weakly on Arabic-script pieces with no leading space, and on common short Arabic
  words (في، على، إلى، عن، و) which are weaker than other word starts.
- On three chat-markup tokens: "</tool_call>" (strongest), "<|im_start|>" and
  "<tool_response>". A check mark "✓" gets a weak response.
- Persian-looking text suppresses the word-start response: if Persian-only letters
  (پ چ ژ گ ک ی) have been seen more recently than Arabic-only ones (ي ك ة), the response
  is cut to 30%.
Everything else is near 0.

State carried from token to token: two decayed counts of recent Arabic-only and
Persian-only letters, reset at each new document.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

CHAT_MARKUP = {"<|im_start|>": 1.9, "</tool_call>": 2.8, "<tool_response>": 1.6}
SHORT_WORDS = {" في": 1.5, " على": 1.5, " إلى": 1.2, " عن": 1.8, " و": 1.5}
CHECK_MARK = 0.9
NOSPACE_ARABIC = 0.6  # Arabic script without a leading space
ALIF = "ا"
NON_JOINING = set("ادذرزو")  # letters that do not connect to a following letter
PERSIAN_ONLY = set("پچژگکی")  # letters Persian uses and Arabic does not
ARABIC_ONLY = set("يكة")  # letters Arabic uses and Persian does not
STRENGTH = {"alif": 0.7, "non_joining": 1.2, "other": 2.8, "persian": 0.2}
PERSIAN_FACTOR = 0.3  # multiplier when recent text looks Persian
DECAY = 0.95  # how fast the recent-language memory fades, per token


def is_arabic(ch):
    return unicodedata.name(ch, "").startswith("ARABIC")


def word_start_strength(first):
    if first == ALIF:
        return STRENGTH["alif"]
    if first in NON_JOINING:
        return STRENGTH["non_joining"]
    if first in PERSIAN_ONLY:
        return STRENGTH["persian"]
    return STRENGTH["other"]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0.0, 0.0)  # new document: forget the language memory
    _, arabic_mem, persian_mem = carry

    value = 0.0
    if token in CHAT_MARKUP:
        value = CHAT_MARKUP[token]
    else:
        if token in SHORT_WORDS:
            value = SHORT_WORDS[token]
        elif token[:1] == " " and len(token) > 1 and is_arabic(token[1]):
            value = word_start_strength(token[1])
        elif "✓" in token:
            value = CHECK_MARK
        elif any(is_arabic(ch) for ch in token):
            value = NOSPACE_ARABIC
        if persian_mem > arabic_mem:
            value *= PERSIAN_FACTOR

    arabic_mem = arabic_mem * DECAY + (1.0 if any(ch in ARABIC_ONLY for ch in token) else 0.0)
    persian_mem = persian_mem * DECAY + (1.0 if any(ch in PERSIAN_ONLY for ch in token) else 0.0)
    return (doc, arabic_mem, persian_mem), value

  "1994-2000", "92-275") about 0.6; after a letter (hyphenated words and file
  names such as "wildfly-client") it is weak, about 0.3.

- " import" right after a "from <module>" line gives about 0.5.

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    after_blank = prev.strip() == ""
